criterion_notes.c1: Examines legal and regulatory frameworks governing residential/consumer drinking water services in Argentina, including judicial protection against disconnection for non-payment and administrative grievance mechanisms for water service users.
criterion_notes.c2: Satisfies BOTH the plain wording of Criterion 2 and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading. Under the plain wording, it examines legal, regulatory, administrative, and judicial governance of water services. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 reading, it addresses rule-type mechanisms directly governing water service continuity and user recourse, including judicial rules prohibiting water disconnection for non-payment, statutory consumer-claim and mandatory conciliation procedures (Ley 24.240, Ley 13.133, Ley 26.993 COPREC), and utility regulatory/enforcement structures (ETOSS, OCABA, ERAS). However, under both readings the overall study decision is exclude because the paper lacks empirical access evidence (Criterion 3 / E05).
criterion_notes.c3: Fails Criterion 3 (E05: No empirical evidence). The paper is a doctrinal comparative legal commentary using legal hermeneutics to review international soft law (UN Guidelines, ISO 26000, Laudato si'), Argentine national and Buenos Aires provincial statutes, and two illustrative appellate amparo rulings, supplemented only by the author's discretionary desk-based scoring (100/100 in Cuadro 1) of two binary questions on whether regulatory agencies formally impose sanctions and initiate investigations. It collects no primary quantitative or qualitative empirical data on households or communities, and explicitly notes on PDF Page 14 that empirical fieldwork on local water cases will be conducted in the future.
criterion_notes.c4: Fails Criterion 4. No empirical outcome measuring household or community water access, connection, continuity, reliability, quantity, affordability, or exclusion is reported; the paper reports only doctrinal and institutional conclusions about regulatory overlap and the formal existence of administrative complaint tools.
criterion_notes.c5: Fails Criterion 5. Because the work is a doctrinal and institutional legal overview rather than an empirical study, there is no identifiable empirical population/sample or measured access outcome linking exposure to household or community service access.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Spanish with an English and Spanish abstract. Per Inclusion Criterion 10, assessment and translation directly from the provided Spanish full text by the screener is feasible; language is not a barrier to evaluation.

evidence_quotes.quote: El objetivo de este trabajo es realizar un análisis comparativo de la normativa vinculada con los usuarios y consumidores aplicables al servicio del agua en los ámbitos internacional, nacional y de la Provincia de Buenos Aires en Argentina.
En ambos casos jurisprudenciales, se ha reconocido explícitamente el derecho de los usuarios a que no les corten el servicio de agua por falta de pago.

Método de la hermenéutica jurídica: se contrastó normativa de dos jurisdicciones de Argentina: nacional y de la Provincia de Buenos Aires, y se analizaron instrumentos internacionales y una selección de casos jurisprudenciales.

Al haberse aplicado solamente una categoría que contiene dos indicadores prácticos no fue posible que los puntajes obtenidos por parte de los indicadores legales sean restados respecto de los que correspondan a los prácticos por la ausencia de los primeros.
Las experiencias prácticas sin duda pueden brindarnos interesantes resultados. En breve nos encontraremos relevando algunos casos en la provincia de Buenos Aires

En especial, en el ámbito nacional, existen nuevas herramientas administrativas para que usuarios y consumidores realicen sus reclamos en relación con la calidad del servicio del agua. Por lo tanto, la existencia del solapamiento normativo no limita el real ejercicio de estos derechos fundamentales.

raw_response.exposure: Consumer and user protection statutes (Ley 24.240, Ley 13.133, Ley 26.993 COPREC), judicial precedents against disconnection for non-payment, and utility regulatory agencies (ETOSS, OCABA, ERAS) in Argentina
raw_response.rationale: Excluded under E05 (No empirical evidence; Exclusion Criterion 1: pure doctrinal commentary without empirical access evidence). Although the paper addresses legal and regulatory mechanisms relevant to residential water service in Argentina (statutory consumer-protection rules, mandatory conciliation via COPREC, judicial precedents barring disconnection for non-payment, and regulatory agencies ETOSS, OCABA, and ERAS), its methodology consists solely of doctrinal legal hermeneutics (comparing statutes, soft-law instruments, and two illustrative court rulings) plus a desk-based authorial scoring of two binary institutional-mandate items (Cuadro 1). It contains no primary qualitative or quantitative empirical data and measures no household or community water-access outcomes, noting explicitly on PDF Page 14 that empirical case studies in Buenos Aires will be conducted in future research.
raw_response.study_design: Doctrinal comparative legal analysis (legal hermeneutics of statutes, soft law, and selected case law) with desk-based scoring of two institutional-mandate indicators
